newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil higher on funds, export talk, meal off.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil higher on funds, export talk, meal off.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were higher at midsession, boosted by fund buying and ideas of export business in the works, traders said.
Soymeal was mostly lower, in line with an early drop in soybeans amid talk China bought South American supplies.

Floor sources cited rumors Taiwan was looking to buy soyoil. They said Taiwan normally bought soybeans to crush into soymeal and soyoil but a cut in the hog herd due to foot and mouth disease sliced demand for soymeal.
Chartists said technical indicators were bullish in soyoil but that soymeal was giving off bearish indications.

Some trade sources also noted expectations that Thursday's U.S. Census Bureau report would reflect a dip in soyoil and soymeal production. Soyoil stocks were at 2.202 million lbs and soymeal at 165,278 tons in the March 27 report

Soymeal futures were pressured by talk China this week bought 200,000 tonnes of South American soymeal, adding to rumors China last week bought 150,000 tonnes of soymeal from South America, traders said.
At 1210 CDT, soymeal futures were down $1.20 per ton to up $1.00 with May down $1.00 at $271.50. Soyoil was up 0.41 to 0.22 cent a lb with May up 0.22 at 24.88 cents.
Funds were noted buyers of soyoil in early trade with Rosenthal Collins said to be a buyer of 800 lots, pit sources said.
